oracle_clues: Bug description: “complex numbers with only imaginary nans get sorted before those with only real nans in descending sorts … they should be sorted after (real nans are the primary key).”

PR#31572 specifies descending compare NaN-handling rules: (1) if greater, only push to right if imaginary part is strictly NaN but the other is not; (2) if less, only push to right if the other imaginary part is strictly NaN but this one is not; (3) if real parts are equal or both are NaN, break the tie by float-like comparison of imaginary; (4) failing all (only one real is NaN), push to the right only if first is NaN.

Code diff (numpy/_core/src/common/numpy_tag.h) changes NaN-aware comparison of the real parts: removes conditions involving `(ra == ra && rb != rb)` / `(ra != ra && rb == rb)` and changes final return from `return ra != ra;` to `return rb != rb;`.

category_specific_evidence: Test constructs complex arrays containing NaNs to check sort behavior: previously used `np.full(100, np.nan + 1j * np.nan, dtype=dtype)` and combinations `im_nans = arange + 1j * nans`, `re_nans = nans + 1j * arange`, `all_nans = nans + 1j * nans`; now builds `im_nans = arange + complex(0, np.nan)`, `re_nans = complex(np.nan, 0) + 1j * arange`, and `all_nans = np.full(100, complex(np.nan, np.nan), dtype=dtype)`.

The fix description states the bug: complex numbers with only imaginary NaNs were getting sorted before those with only real NaNs in descending sorts, and correct NaN semantics require they be sorted after (real NaNs are the primary key).

PR#31572 specifies the ordering/handling logic involving NaNs in the comparator for `greater`/`less` cases: (1) if greater, push to right only if imaginary part is strictly NaN but the other is not; (2) if less, push to right only if the other imaginary part is strictly NaN but this one is not; (3) if real parts are equal or both are NaN, break tie by float-like comparison of imaginary; (4) failing all (only one real part is NaN), push to the right only if first is NaN.

Comparator code change: in `numpy_tag.h` for `complex_type`, handling for NaN-aware comparisons on the real parts was adjusted by removing conditions like `(ra == ra && rb != rb)` and `(ra != ra && rb == rb)`, and changing the final return from `return ra != ra;` to `return rb != rb;`.
